parsed.reason: All three picks are real, named New York venues that a visiting family can simply turn up to: the Children's Museum of Manhattan, the Central Park Zoo and the Brooklyn Children's Museum. Each is sourced to the venue's own organisation, and there are exactly three. None is a term, class session or registration-date programme. CMOM's null price is correct. Its hours note honestly flags a conflict between two of its own pages rather than inventing a resolution. The zoo's prices and seasonal hours ($16.95 child, $22.95 adult, April to October window) and the Brooklyn Children's Museum's $15 admission and Wednesday-to-Sunday schedule look like published figures, not invented ones. The age-fit notes are honest about what each source did and didn't say. Minor points: September 12 to 15 includes Monday and Tuesday, when the Brooklyn Children's Museum is closed. That still leaves two usable days inside the window, so it is not a fault.
